evidence.note: Before any overlay appears, the central diagram is already heavily blurred and faded: no labels are legible, and only faint blue/red strokes and pale box outlines remain.
An opaque white card with a soft drop shadow sits on the left, clearly in focus; the blurred diagram beside it reads as a pale smudge, not an identifiable diagram.
A second opaque card covers the diagram's centre; only faint blurred colour shows through around and behind the cards.
Three opaque shadowed cards cover almost the whole content area; the diagram survives only as ghostly tints between cards and as a blurred legend row below.

rationale: The cards clearly hold focus, with crisp text and a shadow lift, so the overlay does not fight the content. But the blur and fade are so heavy, applied even at step 0 before any overlay, that the diagram beneath can't be recognised: no labels and no structure beyond vague strokes. That matches the fail descriptor 'effects so heavy the context is lost' rather than the reference of an overlay floating above softened but recognisable content.
